message.content:
Cells that contain more than one nucleus are called **multinucleated cells**.  
In biology, such cells are often referred to as a **syncytium** (plural *syncytia*).  

Examples include:

| Cell type | Typical function | Example of multinucleation |
|-----------|------------------|----------------------------|
| Skeletal muscle fiber | Contractile tissue | A single elongated cell with many nuclei along its length |
| Osteoclast | Bone resorption | Large, multinucleated cells that break down bone matrix |
| Certain immune cells | Phagocytosis / inflammation | Multinucleated giant cells seen in granulomas |

So if you’re looking for a general term, “multinucleated cell” or “syncytium” is the correct name.
